title: Family-Owned vs Franchise Real Estate Agents: Which Is Better in South West Sydney?
excerpt: An honest look at the pros and cons of big franchise agencies and small family-owned agents, and how to find a reliable agent whichever you choose.
bodyHtml:
When you start looking for a real estate agent in Liverpool, Campbelltown or anywhere in South West Sydney, you will notice two kinds of agency. There are the big franchise brands with offices in every shopping strip, and there are smaller independent and family-owned agencies run by the person whose name is on the door.

Both can do a good job. They work differently, though, and the right choice depends on what matters most to you. This is an honest comparison from Home7 Real Estate, a family-owned agency in the Liverpool CBD. We will tell you where the big brands genuinely do better, too.

How franchise agencies work

A franchise office is usually a locally owned business that pays to use a national brand. In return it gets the logo, marketing materials, training, systems and a referral network. The office pays the franchisor ongoing fees, typically a share of its income.

Where franchises do well:

  • Brand recognition. Some sellers feel more comfortable with a name they have seen on signboards for years.
  • Bigger teams. More staff can mean more people available for inspections and open homes.
  • Systems and training. Established processes and in-house training for newer agents.
  • Referral networks between offices, which can help if you are moving across Sydney.

Common downsides:

  • Handoffs. The senior agent who wins your listing is not always the person who runs your campaign day to day.
  • Staff turnover. Larger offices often have more junior agents and more change over time.
  • Higher overheads. Franchise fees and brand marketing are costs of running the office, and they can make commission harder to negotiate.
  • Volume. A busy agent juggling many listings has less time for each one.

How family-owned and independent agencies work

An independent agency answers to no head office. The owner usually sets the fees, does much of the selling and leasing personally, and relies on word of mouth and reviews to win the next client.

Where small agencies do well:

  • You deal with the owner. The person you meet at the appraisal is usually the person who sells or manages your property.
  • Lower overheads. No franchise fees means more room for low, flexible commission.
  • Continuity. The same person looks after you for years, across several sales or rentals.
  • Reputation on the line. The owner's name and reviews are the business, so every client matters.

Common downsides:

  • Smaller team. Fewer people, so ask how they cover inspections, holidays and busy weekends.
  • Less brand recognition on signboards, although this matters less than it used to (see below).
  • Coverage. A small agency may focus on a particular region rather than all of Sydney.

Does the brand on the sign affect your sale price?

Less than most people think. The vast majority of buyers and tenants now find properties on realestate.com.au and Domain, where every listing appears side by side in the same format, whatever the brand. A buyer scrolling through three-bedroom houses in Liverpool is comparing the photos, the price and the location, not the agency logo.

What does affect your result is the work behind the listing: an accurate price, good photos, fast follow-up with every enquiry, and strong negotiation when offers come in. Those come down to the individual agent, not the size of the company.

Side-by-side comparison

  • Who you deal with: franchise, often a team or a junior agent. Family-owned, usually the owner.
  • Fees: franchise, often less flexible because of overheads. Family-owned, often lower and more negotiable.
  • Team size: franchise, larger. Family-owned, smaller.
  • Brand recognition: franchise, higher. Family-owned, lower, built on reviews and referrals.
  • Relationship: franchise, can change as staff move on. Family-owned, usually long term.
  • Online exposure: the same for both, on realestate.com.au and Domain.

How to tell if any agent is reliable

Whether you choose a big name or a family business, these checks work the same way:

  1. Check their licence. Every NSW agent must be licensed or registered. You can look them up on the NSW Government's licence check.
  2. Read the reviews. Look at Google reviews for comments about communication, honesty and follow-through, not just a fast sale. Recent reviews count most.
  3. Ask for local results. A reliable agent will happily show you what they have sold or leased near you recently.
  4. Test their response time. Call or email before you sign. How quickly they answer now is a good guide to how quickly they will answer later.
  5. Get everything in writing. Fees, marketing costs and how often you will hear from them.
  6. For rentals, ask about the trust account. NSW agents must hold rent in a trust account and give you regular statements.

Which is right for you?

A franchise may suit you if you want a large team, value a well-known brand, or need an agent who is part of a network across Sydney.

A family-owned agency may suit you if you want to deal with one experienced person from start to finish, want lower and more flexible fees, and value being treated as a person rather than a listing.

About Home7 Real Estate

Home7 is a small, family-owned agency based at Suite 1/209 Macquarie Street in the Liverpool CBD. It is run by our principal, Mohammed Islam, who spent 15 years working with real estate agencies across Sydney before starting his own.

Mohammed started Home7 to offer the experience of a big agency without the big-agency fees. He deals with every client directly and treats them the way he would treat close friends: honest advice, quick replies and regular updates, from the first appraisal until the job is done. Many of our clients have stayed with us for years, across several sales and investment properties.

We sell, lease and manage homes across Liverpool, Campbelltown and South West Sydney. We are rated 4.7 from 44 Google reviews, and clients regularly mention our low fees and communication. One wrote: "Home7 real estate and founder Mr Mohammad is a place of trust. I have been dealing with Mr Mohammad for past 6 years on various occasion."

Frequently asked questions

Are small real estate agencies cheaper than big brands?

Often, because they do not pay franchise fees to a head office. Fees are negotiable at every agency in NSW, though, so compare written quotes. Our guide to real estate agent fees in Liverpool and Campbelltown explains what to expect.

Will a small agency get my property enough exposure?

Yes. Listings from small agencies appear on realestate.com.au and Domain exactly like listings from the big brands, and that is where most buyers and tenants search.

Is a family-owned agent more reliable?

Not automatically. Reliability comes down to the individual agent. A small agency's advantage is that you usually deal with the owner, whose reputation depends on every client. Check reviews, licence and recent local results whichever you choose.

What is the most reliable real estate agent in Liverpool?

Look for an agent with consistent recent Google reviews about communication and honesty, local results you can verify, and fees in writing. Home7 Real Estate is a family-owned Liverpool agency rated 4.7 on Google, where clients deal directly with principal Mohammed Islam.

Talk to us

Comparing agents? Book a free, no-obligation appraisal and meet Mohammed in person. You will get an honest price for your property and a written breakdown of every fee, so you can compare us fairly. For more on choosing, read our guide to real estate agents in Liverpool or our Campbelltown agent guide.

seoDescription: Should you choose a small family-owned real estate agent or a big franchise brand? An honest comparison of service, fees and reliability for sellers and landlords in Liverpool, Campbelltown and South West Sydney.

title: Real Estate Agent Campbelltown NSW: How to Choose the Best One for You (2026)
excerpt: What to look for in a Campbelltown real estate agent, what the 2026 market looks like, and the questions that separate a good local agent from the rest.
bodyHtml:
Campbelltown has changed a lot in the last few years. Prices have climbed toward the million dollar mark, new apartments are going up in the city centre, and buyers who used to look closer to Parramatta or Liverpool are now looking here. That makes choosing the right real estate agent in Campbelltown more important than ever, whether you are selling a family home, renting out an investment or buying your first place.

This guide covers what the Campbelltown market looks like in 2026, what to look for in an agent, what you should expect to pay, and the questions worth asking before you sign. It is written by Home7 Real Estate, a family-owned agency that sells and leases homes across Campbelltown and the Macarthur area from our office in the Liverpool CBD.

The Campbelltown property market in 2026

Different data sources measure the market slightly differently, but they tell the same story:

  • Median house price: roughly $980,000 to $1.07 million for the 2560 postcode, depending on the source and the period measured.
  • Days on market: around 20 to 32 days for houses, which is quick by Sydney standards.
  • Who is buying: young families, first home buyers and investors who want a house with a yard at a price that is no longer possible closer to the city.

A few things keep demand strong. Campbelltown has direct trains to the city on the T8 line, Macarthur Square for shopping, Campbelltown Hospital, and the Western Sydney University campus. ALAND's $400 million, 558-apartment development on Queen Street is reshaping the city centre, and the wider Greater Macarthur growth area, including new communities around Gilead and Menangle Park, is bringing more people to the region.

For sellers, that means a well-priced home can sell quickly. For landlords, rental demand is steady. But it also means the gap between a good agent and an average one shows up quickly in your final price.

You can see local listings and more about the area on our Campbelltown real estate page.

What makes the best real estate agent in Campbelltown?

There is no single best agent for everyone. The best agent for you is the one who can get the right result for your property, at a fair price, and keep you informed the whole way. Look for these five things:

  1. Real local results. Ask which homes they have sold or leased in Campbelltown, Leumeah, Minto, Ingleburn or your own street in the past year. Recent local results beat glossy brochures.
  2. An honest price estimate. A good agent bases their estimate on comparable recent sales and shows you the evidence. Be wary of a price that seems too good to be true. It may just be designed to win your listing.
  3. Clear, fair fees. Commission, marketing and any extras should be in writing before you sign. See our full guide to real estate agent fees in Liverpool and Campbelltown.
  4. Communication you can rely on. You should know who your agent is, how to reach them, and how often you will get updates. Weekly feedback from buyers or tenants is a fair minimum.
  5. Reviews that mention the person, not just the brand. Read Google reviews and look for comments about honesty, responsiveness and negotiation.

Questions to ask a Campbelltown agent before you sign

  • What have you sold or leased near my property recently, and for how much?
  • How did you arrive at your price estimate for my home?
  • What is your commission, does it include GST, and what will marketing cost?
  • Who will I actually be dealing with: you, or someone else in the office?
  • How will you find buyers or tenants beyond the online portals?
  • How often will you update me, and how?
  • What happens if I want to end the agreement?

Remember that in NSW you have a cooling-off period on a residential sales agency agreement. You can cancel it in writing until 5pm on the next business day or Saturday after signing.

Red flags to watch for

  • A price estimate far above every other agent's, with no comparable sales to back it up.
  • Pressure to sign on the spot.
  • Marketing costs described as "to be confirmed".
  • You meet the senior agent once, then get handed to someone junior.
  • Calls and emails that go unanswered for days.

Selling or leasing in Campbelltown with Home7

Home7 Real Estate is a small, family-owned agency led by our principal, Mohammed Islam. Before founding Home7, Mohammed spent 15 years working with real estate agencies across Sydney, and he now handles sales, leasing and property management for clients across South West Sydney, including the Macarthur area.

We have sold homes in Campbelltown and Leumeah and leased more than 20 properties across Campbelltown, Leumeah, Ingleburn, Minto and Ambarvale. You can see recent results on our sold and leased pages.

What clients tell us they value most:

  • You deal with Mohammed directly, from appraisal to settlement or lease signing, instead of being passed around an office.
  • Low, negotiable fees, agreed in writing before anything is signed, with no franchise overheads built in.
  • Honest pricing based on real local sales, even when it is not the biggest number you have heard.
  • Quick replies and regular updates, so you always know what is happening with your property.

Our office is at Suite 1/209 Macquarie Street, Liverpool, around half an hour from Campbelltown, and we come to you for appraisals and inspections. For more on why sellers choose us, see five reasons Campbelltown sellers choose Home7.

What our clients say

Home7 is rated 4.7 from 44 Google reviews. A few in our clients' own words:

  • "The team at Home7 Real Estate is amazing. Fast service, low cost, and excellent communication. Mohammed is the best agent I've worked with."
  • "Mohammed is professional, honest, and highly knowledgeable about the local property market. His communication, negotiation skills, and attention to detail made the entire process smooth and stress-free."
  • "Best property management service I've experienced! Home7 Real Estate offers great value with low charges and excellent communication."

Frequently asked questions

Who is the best real estate agent in Campbelltown?

The best agent for you is one with recent results near your property, an honest price estimate backed by comparable sales, fees in writing, and a track record of good communication in their reviews. Interview two or three local agents and compare them. Home7 Real Estate is a family-owned agency that sells and leases across Campbelltown, rated 4.7 on Google for its low fees, honesty and communication.

How much do real estate agents charge in Campbelltown?

Commission in South West Sydney is commonly around 1.8% to 2.5% of the sale price, plus marketing. Property management is usually 5% to 8% of rent plus a letting fee. Fees are negotiable in NSW, so always get a written quote.

Is it a good time to sell in Campbelltown?

Houses in Campbelltown have been selling in roughly three to five weeks in 2026, and buyer demand from families and investors remains steady. The right timing depends on your plans and your property, and a free appraisal is the easiest way to find out what your home is worth today.

Do I need a Campbelltown-based agent?

Local knowledge matters more than an office address. What counts is whether the agent has recently sold or leased homes near yours, knows the buyers in your price range, and will be there for inspections. Ask to see their recent local results.

Does Home7 manage rental properties in Campbelltown?

Yes. We look after tenant screening, leases, rent collection, routine inspections and repairs for landlords across Campbelltown, Leumeah, Minto, Ingleburn and nearby suburbs.

Get an honest appraisal

Thinking about selling or renting out your Campbelltown property? Book a free, no-obligation market appraisal with Mohammed. You will get an honest price range based on real local sales and a clear, written breakdown of every fee. If you are also comparing agents in Liverpool, our Liverpool agent guide covers that side of the region.

bodyHtml:
Picking a real estate agent in Liverpool NSW is one of the biggest money decisions in any sale or rental. The right agent can add tens of thousands to your sale price or keep a good tenant in your investment for years. The wrong one can cost you weeks on the market and a price you didn't need to accept.

This guide covers what a good Liverpool agent actually does, what it should cost, the questions worth asking before you sign anything, and the red flags to watch for. It also explains how we work at Home7 Real Estate, a family-owned agency based at Suite 1/209 Macquarie Street in the Liverpool CBD, so you can compare us fairly against anyone else you're talking to.

What a real estate agent in Liverpool does for you

A good local agent is more than someone who lists your home online. Depending on what you need, they should handle:

  • Selling: pricing your home against recent comparable sales, preparing it for market, photography and portal listings on realestate.com.au and Domain, running inspections, and negotiating with buyers through to exchange and settlement.
  • Property management: finding and screening tenants, leases, rent collection, routine inspections, repairs with trusted local tradespeople, and keeping you compliant with NSW tenancy law.
  • Leasing: getting a vacant property rented quickly at the right weekly rent.
  • Buying: helping buyers understand values street by street, and in some cases acting for the buyer through a buyers advisory service.
  • Appraisals: an honest opinion of what your property would sell or rent for today, backed by real local sales.

Why a local Liverpool agent matters

Liverpool is not one market. A unit near Liverpool station, a family home in Casula or Prestons, and a new build in Austral, Leppington or Edmondson Park attract different buyers and sell on different timelines. An agent who works these streets every week knows who is buying, what similar homes actually sold for (not just what they were listed at), and which features local buyers will pay more for.

Local knowledge also shows up in the small things: knowing which school catchments families ask about, how close a home is to the hospital, the train line or Westfield, and how the Western Sydney Airport and new estates to the west are shifting demand. For current prices and suburb trends, see our Liverpool real estate market guide.

How much does a real estate agent cost in Liverpool?

Agent fees in NSW are not fixed by law. They are agreed between you and the agent and written into the agency agreement. Selling fees in Sydney are commonly a commission of roughly 1.5% to 2.5% of the sale price, plus a separate marketing budget for photos, portal listings and signage. Property management is usually charged as a percentage of the rent collected, plus a letting fee when a new tenant is found.

A few things worth knowing:

  • The lowest fee is not always the cheapest outcome. A slightly higher fee from an agent who negotiates harder can still leave you with more money.
  • Ask exactly what is included in the marketing budget and whether you pay it if the property doesn't sell.
  • Get every fee in writing before you sign.

At Home7 our fees are low and negotiable, and we give you the full breakdown during your free market appraisal, with no hidden costs.

Questions to ask before you choose an agent

  1. What have you sold or leased near me recently, and for how much? Ask for real addresses and results, not general claims.
  2. How did you arrive at your price estimate? A good agent shows you the comparable sales behind the number.
  3. Who will I actually deal with? Some agencies sign you up with a senior agent and hand you to a junior.
  4. What is your marketing plan, and what does it cost?
  5. How often will you update me? Weekly feedback from buyers or tenants should be the minimum.
  6. How long is the agency agreement, and how do I end it?

Red flags to watch for

  • A price that sounds too good. Some agents quote high to win your listing, then push you to drop the price weeks later. In NSW, the estimated selling price must be written into the agency agreement and an agent must not advertise a property below it, so ask how they got to that number.
  • Pressure to sign on the spot. A good agent is happy for you to compare.
  • No licence details. Every agent selling or managing property in NSW must be licensed. You can check a licence on the NSW Fair Trading website.
  • Vague answers about fees. If it isn't in writing, it isn't agreed.
  • Slow replies before you've even signed. It rarely gets better after.

How Home7 works as your Liverpool agent

Home7 Real Estate is a family-owned agency founded by Mohammed, who still works directly with clients. We are not a big franchise, and we like it that way: you deal with the same people from your first call to settlement or lease signing, and we pick up the phone.

  • Sales: honest pricing from local comparable sales, professional photography, listings on realestate.com.au and Domain, open homes and firm negotiation. See properties we have sold.
  • Property management and leasing: careful tenant screening, routine inspections with reports, on-time rent and quick repairs. See properties we have leased.
  • Buyers: current properties for sale and properties for rent, plus open for inspection times.
  • Free appraisals: find out what your home would sell or rent for with a free, no-obligation appraisal.

You can meet the team and read about each agent before you call.

Suburbs we cover

Our office is in the Liverpool CBD and most of our work is in and around the Liverpool area, including Liverpool, Casula, Warwick Farm, Prestons, Moorebank, Edmondson Park, Austral and Leppington, as well as Campbelltown and the wider South West Sydney area.

What our clients say

We are rated 4.7 from 44 Google reviews. A few of them, word for word:

"Excellent experience with Home7 Real Estate. Mohammed is professional, honest, and highly knowledgeable about the local property market. His communication, negotiation skills, and attention to detail made the entire process smooth and stress-free."

James Smith, Google review

"Home7 real estate and founder Mr Mohammad is a place of trust. I have been dealing with Mr Mohammad for past 6 years on various occasion. Mohammad has helped and still helping us in sales, managing my investment property."

M S B Islam, Google review

"Best property management service I've experienced! Home7 Real Estate offers great value with low charges and excellent communication."

MD Jubayer Hossen, Google review

Frequently asked questions

Who is the best real estate agent in Liverpool NSW?

There is no single best agent for everyone. The best agent for you is one with recent results near your property, a clear and honest price estimate, fees in writing, and someone you trust to answer the phone. Talk to two or three agents and compare them using the questions above.

How much does it cost to sell a house in Liverpool?

Expect agent commission (commonly around 1.5% to 2.5% in Sydney), a marketing budget, and conveyancing or solicitor fees. Ask any agent for a full written breakdown before you sign.

How long does it take to sell a home in Liverpool?

It depends on the property, the price and the time of year. A well-priced home with good marketing usually sells within a few weeks of going live. Overpricing is the most common reason a home sits on the market.

Do you manage rental properties in Liverpool?

Yes. We manage rentals across Liverpool and South West Sydney, covering tenant selection, leases, rent collection, inspections and maintenance.

How do I contact Home7 Real Estate?

Call us on (02) 8729 7753, email admin@home7.com.au, or visit our office at Suite 1/209 Macquarie Street, Liverpool NSW 2170. We are open Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm and Saturday 9am to 4pm. You can also send us a message or book a free appraisal online.

title: Real Estate Agent Liverpool NSW: How to Choose the Right One

bodyHtml:
Liverpool is changing faster than almost anywhere in Sydney. A new international airport opens on its doorstep in October 2026. The population is forecast to jump by more than 50% by 2041. The CBD is being rebuilt around a university, a hospital precinct and a new transport spine.

This guide gives you the facts, the numbers and the local knowledge behind real estate in Liverpool NSW, whether you're a first-home buyer, an investor, an upsizer or an owner thinking about selling.

Last updated: September 2026. We refresh this page as the market and major projects move.

Liverpool real estate at a glance

  • Houses: a 3-bedroom house has a median of about $1.15 million and a 4-bedroom about $1.28 million (realestate.com.au suburb data).
  • Units: mostly under $600,000, which is why Liverpool is one of NSW's busiest first-home-buyer postcodes.
  • Rents: around $650 a week for houses and $520–$540 for units.
  • Yields: roughly 3% for houses, 5.5–5.8% for units.
  • Distance: about 27 km south-west of the Sydney CBD, on the train line and the M5/M7 motorways.

Figures are approximate and come from realestate.com.au and public sales and rental data. Medians move every month, so ask us for the number that matters: your property's.

Why everyone is watching Liverpool

1. The airport is real, and it's days away

  • Western Sydney International (Nancy-Bird Walton) Airport opens to passengers on 25 October 2026, with freight from July 2026.
  • It's a $5.3 billion project. The airport company's head office is in Liverpool's city centre.
  • The wider Aerotropolis is expected to support around 200,000 jobs across the Western Parkland City over time.

2. Liverpool gets its own airport link

  • The Sydney Metro Western Sydney Airport line (St Marys to the airport) is due in 2027, but it doesn't stop at Liverpool.
  • Liverpool's connection is the Fifteenth Avenue Smart Transit (FAST) corridor: a dedicated rapid-transit route with over $1 billion committed. Major works are expected from around 2027.
  • Better access to the airport and Bradfield is a big reason investors are watching Liverpool's fringe suburbs.

3. A city that is growing up

  • Liverpool LGA's population is around 285,000 today and forecast to reach about 440,000 by 2041.
  • Planners expect roughly 2,700 new dwellings a year on average, reaching about 131,000 homes by 2041.
  • Higher densities are focused on the CBD and areas with good transport.

The Liverpool CBD is being rebuilt

  • Liverpool Civic Place: a major mixed-use precinct. The University of Wollongong is moving in, with further stages targeted for around 2028.
  • Health: Liverpool Hospital is one of the biggest employers in South West Sydney, and it keeps growing. Healthcare workers need homes nearby.
  • Education: university and TAFE campuses bring students, staff and rental demand.
  • Public space: upgrades to George and Moore Streets and the 28-hectare Woodward Park project are lifting how the city feels.

Why it matters: jobs, study and healthcare in one place are what create lasting property demand, not just a short-term buzz.

Council strategy and the rules that shape prices

  • Council's housing strategy: Liverpool City Council directs the highest densities to the CBD and areas with good transport, and keeps many established suburbs lower-density.
  • State planning reforms: NSW's low and mid-rise reforms open up more housing types near stations and centres. That can lift land value on well-located blocks.
  • Granny flats: state rules make secondary dwellings easier to approve, which changes what a large block is worth.
  • Foreign buyers: NSW charges an extra surcharge purchaser duty (9% at last check) and restrictions currently apply to foreign buyers of established homes. Rules change, so get advice before you buy from overseas.
  • What it means for you: two identical houses on different streets can have very different potential. Zoning is the hidden variable.

Liverpool: past, present and future

  • 1810: Liverpool is founded by Governor Macquarie, making it one of Australia's oldest towns.
  • Today: a regional city with a hospital, university presence, Westfield and a busy rail hub.
  • July and October 2026: Western Sydney Airport opens for freight, then passengers.
  • 2027: the Metro line to the airport is due, and major FAST corridor works are expected to begin.
  • Around 2028: further stages of Liverpool Civic Place are targeted.
  • 2041: population forecast of around 440,000.

How the property landscape is changing

High-rise apartments in the CBD

  • The CBD has the most apartment growth in the region.
  • Older units can still be found for under $500,000. New-build prices are higher.
  • Investors see stronger yields on units, but supply matters. Ask us how much new stock is coming before you buy.

Townhouses, terraces and low-rise

  • NSW's low and mid-rise housing reforms allow more terraces, townhouses, manor houses and low-rise apartments near stations and town centres.
  • Rules vary by street and zone. Check the council's mapping before you plan anything.

Bigger blocks and granny flats

  • A secondary dwelling ("granny flat") can be up to 60 square metres and must sit on the same lot as a main house.
  • Blocks of around 450 sqm or more are typically the target, so confirm your lot with a certifier.
  • A granny flat can add rental income, or space for family. Many Liverpool owners now buy with this in mind.

The Liverpool buyer profile

  • First-home buyers: Liverpool (2170) has repeatedly ranked at or near the top of NSW for first-home-buyer sales.
  • NSW first-home concessions: stamp duty is waived on eligible homes up to $800,000, with a sliding concession up to $1 million.
  • Federal 5% deposit scheme: lets eligible first-home buyers buy with a much smaller deposit. Check current caps and eligibility.
  • Investors: attracted by yields, jobs and infrastructure.
  • Diverse community: Liverpool is one of Sydney's most multicultural cities, with strong Vietnamese, Arabic, Indian, Nepali and Pacific communities, plus many international students. That shapes demand for everything from apartments to multi-generational family homes.

Read next: the best suburbs to buy in Liverpool and how the 5% deposit scheme works.

Where prices are heading (an honest view)

  • The bull case: the airport, Aerotropolis jobs, population growth and better transport support long-term demand.
  • The caution: Liverpool's strong run means the easy gains may be behind us. Vacancy has eased in some investor-heavy pockets since the very tight levels of 2025.
  • The takeaway: the right property in the right pocket matters more than the postcode alone.

Thinking of timing? Read Is now a good time to invest in Sydney property? and our 2026 market outlook.

Suburbs to watch around Liverpool

Liverpool's surrounding suburbs often tell the more interesting story. Approximate 12-month house medians from public data (small sample sizes, so use as a guide only):

  • Warwick Farm: around $930,000. One of the lower prices near the CBD and station, with the racecourse precinct nearby. Warwick Farm guide.
  • Lurnea: around $1.15 million. Family suburb close to Liverpool with steady growth.
  • Hoxton Park: around $1.1 million. Newer estates and a recent price reset in some data, worth a closer look.
  • Middleton Grange: around $1.2 million. Modern family housing with solid growth.
  • Edmondson Park: around $1.3 million. Master-planned, with its own station and town centre.
  • Austral: around $1.1–1.2 million and one of the fastest-growing suburbs in the region, with new estates and land still being released.
  • Leppington: around $1.2–1.35 million. It has its own station and is being built out as a major centre.
  • Moorebank: around $1.45 million. Premium end of the market, plus a major freight and employment hub.
  • Prestons and Casula: Prestons and Casula are popular with families who want space near Liverpool.

Are Edmondson Park, Austral and Leppington part of Liverpool?

  • Austral is in the City of Liverpool.
  • Leppington and Edmondson Park are shared: part of each suburb sits in the City of Liverpool, and the rest in Camden (Leppington) or Campbelltown (Edmondson Park).
  • Liverpool Council has dedicated planning programs for these growth areas, and Liverpool's population forecast includes them.
  • They sit in Sydney's South West Growth Area, so they're the newer, hotter end of the market, with new estates and infrastructure catching up.

How to find the "hidden" pockets

  • Look for suburbs within a short trip of a station or the future FAST corridor.
  • Look for older homes on larger blocks. They give you options to renovate, add a granny flat or redevelop.
  • Compare price per square metre of land, not just the headline price.
  • Check what's being approved next door. New supply can help or hurt.

Looking further out? See development land in Austral and homes in the Liverpool area.

Liverpool real estate: quick answers

Is Liverpool a good place to buy property?

It has strong fundamentals: jobs, a hospital, a university, the airport and transport upgrades, plus relatively accessible prices for Sydney. As always, the right property matters as much as the suburb.

What is the median house price in Liverpool NSW?

Based on realestate.com.au data, a 3-bedroom house has a median of about $1.15 million and a 4-bedroom about $1.28 million. Units are mostly under $600,000. Figures change monthly.

Is Liverpool good for investors?

Units have offered yields of around 5.5–5.8%, and rental demand has been strong. Vacancy and supply need watching, especially in the CBD.

How much does a real estate agent cost in Liverpool?

Commission is negotiable and varies by property and campaign. Ask for a written fee and marketing plan before you sign.

How do I choose a real estate agent in Liverpool?

Look at recent sales in your street, ask how they'll market your home, check reviews and make sure they're licensed. Local knowledge and clear communication matter most.
